title: How To Change A Student's Life
author: Michael Linsin
summary: In a personal reflection, Linsin describes how strong classroom management creates the time, trust, and rapport needed for teachers to truly know their students and, at times, change the course of their lives. He credits his own high school English teacher, Bill Heyde, who recently passed away, with recognizing a communication ability in him that he could not see in himself, and with shaping his eventual career as a teacher and the philosophy behind Smart Classroom Management. Linsin frames the ability to notice untapped potential in students as something that cannot be forced or manufactured — it emerges naturally once a teacher has built the kind of relationship that lets a student's true self surface. He challenges readers to actively look for that "one thing" in their own students, arguing that exceptional classroom management is what makes such recognition possible in the first place. The article closes with a call to spend time cultivating that noticing ability through ongoing study of SCM's materials.
points: Strong classroom management provides the time, trust, and freedom from distraction needed to truly know one's students.
Rapport and likability built through consistent management form the basis for a teacher's lasting influence on a student's life.
A teacher's recognition of a student's hidden ability is not manufactured — it is noticed once real trust and relationship exist.
Linsin credits his own high school teacher, Bill Heyde, with seeing an ability in him he could not see in himself, shaping his career.
The goal for teachers is to notice, not manufacture, the unique gift in a student and help it surface naturally over time.
quotes: You’ll have the trust and likability that breaks down walls and frees them to be themselves around you.
It’s an ability that can change lives, sometimes dramatically, and set a student on a new and better and often redemptive course they never would have found on their own.
As a freshman in high school, I was lost and disillusioned. I was a Gordian knot of shyness and fear and in profound need of direction.
I always have enjoyed finding the students who were good but didn’t know they were good and challenge them to push themselves up.
He saw something in me no one else was able to see, including myself, and it changed me forever.
Exceptional classroom management allows you to build the kind of trusting relationships that reveal who your students are and the unique gifts they can offer the world.
It liberates their abilities lying dormant within, which bubble to the surface and then burst forth in a bright, glowing supernova you can’t help but recognize.
